event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: CDW’s 2023 Form 10-K links the COVID-19 pandemic to a broad array of concrete and continuing risks that have already affected – and are expected to keep affecting – the company’s operations, finances and supply chain.  The filing describes direct, realised impacts (e.g., supply-chain bottlenecks, labour disruptions, rising logistics costs and inflation) alongside forward-looking uncertainties (resurgences, new variants, macro-economic recession, government budget cuts).  Language is largely specific rather than boiler-plate: it enumerates backlogs at vendors, inflationary pressures the company may not be able to pass through, possible closures of distribution centres, and exposure of critical co-workers.  Because the filing date (24 Feb 2023) is within three years of the WHO pandemic declaration (11 Mar 2020), the Time-Decay Principle permits high severity scores.  Overall, the disclosure depicts an elevated, multi-faceted risk landscape that remains current; none of the sentences offer meaningful mitigation offsets, so individual evidence pieces receive robust positive scores (generally 4-9, capped at 10) to reflect the recent timing, specificity and already-realised impacts.

evidence_list.snippet: The outbreak of the novel coronavirus (“COVID-19”) pandemic has adversely impacted and could continue to adversely impact our business and results of operations and could also adversely impact our cash flows, financial condition and liquidity.

components.reason: States that COVID-19 has already adversely impacted the company.
Forecasts the adverse impact will continue.
Covers multiple financial dimensions (cash flows, liquidity, results of operations).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct statement of realised and continuing harm across several financial metrics warrants a high recent-event score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: The global spread of COVID-19 continues to create significant macroeconomic uncertainty, volatility and disruption.

components.reason: Identifies ongoing, not past, disruption from the pandemic.
Uses strong qualifiers (“significant”, “volatility”).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights persistent macro-level instability but without company-specific quantification, giving a moderate risk score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced and could continue to experience disruptions, including as a result of resurgences of COVID-19, that prevent us from meeting the demands of our customers, such as product constraints from our vendor partners and wholesale distributors and other disruptions to our supply chain, disruptions in or restrictions on the ability of our coworkers to work effectively, temporary closures of our distribution facilities, modifications in the operation of facilities that remain open and disruptions of commercial delivery services.

components.reason: Confirms company has already experienced disruptions.
Projects ongoing risk from future resurgences.
Enumerates multiple concrete operational impacts (supply chain, labour, facilities, logistics).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Detailed list of past and potential future operational breakdowns merits a high score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: The impact of COVID-19 and measures implemented to slow the spread have caused and could continue to cause delay in, or limit the ability of, our customers to place orders for our products and services and make timely payments to us and could materially increase our labor, logistics and other costs.

components.reason: Indicates actual customer order/payment delays already occurred.
Notes future continuation of these problems.
Specifies material cost inflation in labour and logistics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Links pandemic to revenue collection risk and cost inflation, justifying a strong score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: As long as the pandemic continues, our coworkers will continue to be exposed to health risks, and we could be negatively impacted in the future if a significant number of our coworkers, or coworkers who perform critical functions, become unable to work as a result of exposure to COVID-19.

components.reason: Highlights potential workforce availability risk tied to ongoing health exposure.
Points out vulnerability of critical functions.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Focuses on prospective labour-force threat without current impact data, earning a lower (but still positive) score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: During the COVID-19 pandemic and even after it has subsided, we may experience adverse impacts to our business as a result of the pandemic’s global economic impact, including any recession, economic downturn or volatility, government spending cuts, tightening of credit markets or increased unemployment that has occurred or may occur in the future, which could cause our customers and potential customers to postpone or reduce spending on technology products or services or put downward pressure on prices.

components.reason: Identifies broad economic transmission mechanisms (recession, credit tightening).
Connects macro effects to reduced customer demand and pricing pressure.
Covers post-pandemic tail-risk period.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Describes medium-term demand risk channels, yielding a moderate score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, we have experienced and may continue to experience inflationary pressures, resulting in increased product prices that we may be unable to pass on to our customers.

components.reason: Acknowledges realised inflationary cost pressure linked to pandemic environment.
Admits possible margin squeeze from inability to pass through costs.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Covers cost-side risk but is narrower in scope, so score is 3.

evidence_list.snippet: The extent to which the COVID-19 pandemic impacts our business, results of operations, cash flows, financial condition and liquidity in the future will depend on future developments, which are uncertain and cannot be predicted, including, but not limited to, the ultimate duration of the pandemic, future resurgences and emergences of new variants of the virus and their severity, the availability, efficacy and acceptance of vaccines and treatments, actions taken to contain the virus including reimplementation of closures, and the effectiveness of these actions, and to what extent normal economic and operating conditions can resume and be sustained.

components.reason: Emphasises high degree of unpredictability and dependency on external factors.
Covers multiple contingencies (variants, vaccines, closures), signalling persistent uncertainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking uncertainty without concrete quantification gives a modest score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: Periods of increased demand on delivery services, such as those we have experienced during the COVID-19 pandemic, could materially adversely affect our ability to deliver or receive products on a timely basis.

components.reason: Specifies logistic bottlenecks already experienced.
Links to material adverse effect on timeliness.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Narrow operational impact (shipping) produces a score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: Manufacturing interruptions or delays, including as a result of ... pandemics (such as the COVID-19 pandemic) ... could disrupt our supply chain.

components.reason: Explicitly names pandemics as a trigger for manufacturing interruptions.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic, hypothetical supply-chain reference earns a minimal positive score of 1.

evidence_list.snippet: As the duration and ongoing economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic remain uncertain, current and future budget priorities and funding levels for Government, Healthcare and Education customers may be adversely affected.

components.reason: Points to sector-specific demand risk tied to pandemic uncertainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights possible public-sector spending cuts; limited detail results in score of 2.

evidence_list.snippet: Individually and collectively, the consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic have adversely impacted and could continue to adversely impact our business and results of operations and could also adversely impact our cash flows, financial condition and liquidity.

components.reason: Restates realised adverse impact across multiple financial areas.
Affirms continuation of these impacts.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad reaffirmation of multi-faceted harm yields a solid score of 6.
